title: The smooth wavefront set
notes: \((x_0,\xi_0)\notin\mathrm{WF}(u)\) when a cutoff \(\varphi(x_0)\ne0\) makes \(\widetilde{u\varphi}\) rapidly decreasing in an angular neighbourhood of \(\xi_0\).
statement: We use \(\widehat u(\xi)=\int e^{-ix\cdot\xi}u(x)\,dx\) throughout the microlocal reconstruction. For an open \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(u\in\mathcal D'(\Omega)\), a nonzero covector \((x_0,\xi_0)\) is outside \(\mathrm{WF}(u)\) iff some \(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)\), equal to one near \(x_0\), and an open cone \(V\ni\xi_0\) satisfy \(\sup_{\xi\in V}(1+|\xi|)^N|\widehat{\varphi u}(\xi)|<\infty\) for every integer \(N\ge0\).
fate: Published in \citet[Definition 2.5.2 and pp.~121--122]{hormander1971fourier} in 1971; the equivalent Fourier description is explicit on p.~122. Earlier seminar occurrences are 1971-234.1 and 1973-329.1.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Gelfand’s hyperplane slicing interpretation
notes: Gelfand relates the smoothness of a one-variable integral over parallel hyperplanes to membership of the normal covector in the wavefront.
statement: For a compactly supported localized distribution \(v=\chi u\), the pushforward under \(x\mapsto x\cdot\theta\) has one-dimensional Fourier transform \(\widehat v(t\theta)\). Absence from \(\mathrm{WF}(u)\) requires such rapid decay uniformly for \(\theta\) in an angular neighbourhood and with localization near \(x_0\). A single unlocalized slice integral cannot detect every covector, because cancellations are possible.
reconstruction: The cutoff, angular uniformity, and warning about cancellation make precise the one-line analogy; they are editorial qualifications.
fate: The precise directional statement follows from the Fourier characterization in \citet[p.~122]{hormander1971fourier}; this repeats the explanatory intervention 1973-329.3. It is an interpretation of an old definition, not an asserted new inversion theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: One-sided analytic continuation and directional regularity
notes: For \(\xi_0>0\), the notes give \(u=\varphi+u_1\) locally, with \(\varphi\in C_c^\infty\) and \(u_1\) continuing analytically into the upper half-plane.
statement: A holomorphic function in an upper half-disc with at most polynomial growth towards the boundary has a distributional boundary value. With \(\widehat u(\xi)=\int e^{-ix\xi}u(x)\,dx\), its smooth wavefront has only positive covectors on the boundary interval, and therefore excludes negative covectors; adding a smooth function does not change this. Reversing the Fourier convention reverses the sign. The notebook specifies neither that convention nor the boundary-value growth condition, so its positive-half-ray wording is not by itself a convention-independent contradiction.
reconstruction: We give a sufficient distributional-boundary-value statement, with polynomial growth and the same negative-exponent Fourier transform as the rest of the chapter. The notebook's upper-half-plane and positive-excluded-ray wording can agree only with the opposite transform convention; no such convention is recorded.
fate: The item is an expository boundary-value interpretation of the wavefront framework in \citet[Section 2.5]{hormander1971fourier}, not an exact theorem quotation established from that paper. An independent explicit sign check is \citet[Appendix A, equation (A.4) and following calculation]{bohrlefeuvrepaternain2024invariant}: \(\mathrm{WF}((x+i0)^{-1})=\{(0,\xi):\xi>0\}\). The modern check does not establish a new historical priority or verify an unqualified converse in the notebook.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Projection onto singular support
notes: \(\pi(\mathrm{WF}(u))=\operatorname{sing\,supp}u\), with \(\pi:T^*\Omega\to\Omega\).
statement: For every distribution on a smooth manifold, the base projection of its smooth wavefront set is exactly its singular support.
fate: \citet[Theorem 2.5.3]{hormander1971fourier}, published 1971, is an exact match. The earlier occurrence is 1973-329.4.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Frequency projection and rapid Fourier decay
notes: \(\pi'\mathrm{WF}(u)\) is called the smallest closed cone outside which the Fourier transform decreases rapidly.
statement: For \(u\in\mathcal E'(\mathbb R^n)\), let \(K=\{\xi\ne0:\exists x,\ (x,\xi)\in\mathrm{WF}(u)\}\). Then \(K\) is closed in \(\mathbb R^n\setminus0\), and \(\widehat u\) decreases faster than every power in each closed cone disjoint from \(K\). Conversely, this property determines the smallest such closed cone. For a general local distribution apply the statement to compactly supported localizations.
reconstruction: Compact support is supplied from the cited theorem.
fate: Exact compact-support version: \citet[Proposition 2.5.5]{hormander1971fourier}. Compact support is missing in the notebook; without a suitable global hypothesis even an ordinary Fourier transform need not be defined.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Multiplication under the no-opposite-covectors condition
notes: For \(\mathcal D'_\Gamma=\{u:\mathrm{WF}(u)\subset\Gamma\}\), and \(\Gamma_1+\Gamma_2\) avoiding zero, the notes give a bilinear map into \(\mathcal D'_{(\Gamma_1+\Gamma_2)\cup\Gamma_1\cup\Gamma_2}\).
statement: If \(u,v\in\mathcal D'(\Omega)\) and there is no \((x,\xi)\in\mathrm{WF}(u)\) with \((x,-\xi)\in\mathrm{WF}(v)\), their product is canonically defined by pullback of \(u\otimes v\) to the diagonal. Its wavefront is contained in \(\mathrm{WF}(u)\cup\mathrm{WF}(v)\cup\{(x,\xi+\eta):(x,\xi)\in\mathrm{WF}(u),(x,\eta)\in\mathrm{WF}(v)\}\).
reconstruction: No continuity claim for an unspecified topology on the open-cone spaces is added.
fate: \citet[Theorem 2.5.10]{hormander1971fourier} proves the closed-cone version, predating the talk. The occurrence 1973-329.11 has the same criterion. The notebook calls its containing cones open; the pointwise noncancellation criterion remains the decisive condition.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: A distribution kernel defines an operator
notes: \(A\in\mathcal D'(\Omega_x\times\Omega_y)\) is paired with \(u(y)v(x)\), defining \(A:C_c^\infty(\Omega_y)\to\mathcal D'(\Omega_x)\).
statement: A distribution \(K\) on \(X\times Y\), with densities understood, defines a continuous linear operator by \(\langle Au,v\rangle=\langle K,v\otimes u\rangle\). Conversely every continuous operator \(C_c^\infty(Y)\to\mathcal D'(X)\) has a unique Schwartz kernel.
reconstruction: Continuity and the density convention are stated explicitly.
fate: This is the established Schwartz kernel formalism used in \citet[\S2.5, before Theorem 2.5.12]{hormander1971fourier}; earlier occurrence 1973-329.5.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Kernel extensions with both axis wavefronts absent
notes: If \(\mathrm{WF}(A)\) has no points with \(\xi=0\) or \(\eta=0\), then \(A:C_c^\infty(Y)\to C^\infty(X)\) and \(A:\mathcal E'(Y)\to\mathcal D'(X)\).
statement: For \(K\in\mathcal D'(X\times Y)\), assume \(\mathrm{WF}(K)\) avoids both sets \(\{(x,\xi;y,0):\xi\ne0\}\) and \(\{(x,0;y,\eta):\eta\ne0\}\). Kernel action then maps tests to smooth functions and extends canonically and continuously to compactly supported distributions. Proper support is needed only for corresponding noncompact-input or compact-output assertions.
fate: \citet[Theorems 2.5.12--2.5.14]{hormander1971fourier} establish these operations. This repeats 1973-329.6.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: The primed relation and propagation through a kernel
notes: \(\mathrm{WF}'(A)=\{(x,\xi;y,-\eta):(x,\xi;y,\eta)\in\mathrm{WF}(A)\}\), and \(\mathrm{WF}(Au)\subset\mathrm{WF}'(A)\circ\mathrm{WF}(u)\).
statement: Under the no-axis assumptions of the preceding item, for every \(u\in\mathcal E'(Y)\), \(\mathrm{WF}(Au)\subset\{(x,\xi):\exists(y,\eta)\in\mathrm{WF}(u),\ (x,\xi;y,\eta)\in\mathrm{WF}'(K)\}\). The minus sign belongs to the input covector of the kernel.
fate: Exact statement in \citet[Theorem 2.5.14]{hormander1971fourier}; compare 1973-329.7--8. The preceding assumptions must remain attached to this shorthand formula.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Gelfand proposes polynomial as well as linear integration
notes: \ru{Идея Г.} is followed by integrating linear functions and polynomials; a curved outline is cut by parallel segments.
statement: The evidence supports a proposal to replace linear level sets by polynomial ones in an integral-geometric construction. It does not identify the family of polynomials, the integration measure, a target space, or an inversion or range question. Thus it determines no unique theorem or problem.
fate: Generalized Radon transforms are thematically related to the canonical-relation calculus of \citet[\S4.1]{hormander1971fourier}, but that relation does not identify this particular proposal. The scan does not justify reading the small sketch as a specified polynomial transform.
present_status: As of November 2026: the precise intended construction is not recoverable from this entry; no claim of an undeveloped idea is made.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Composition of wavefront relations
notes: For \(A:\mathcal E'(Y)\to\mathcal D'(X)\), \(B:\mathcal E'(Z)\to\mathcal E'(Y)\), the notes write \(\mathrm{WF}'(A\circ B)\subset\mathrm{WF}'(A)\circ\mathrm{WF}'(B)\).
statement: For properly supported distribution kernels whose wavefronts avoid both coordinate axes, composition is defined and its primed wavefront lies in the composite canonical relation. More generally one needs the wavefront transversality condition at the intermediate variable and must include the horizontal and vertical error sets when these are nonempty.
reconstruction: The earlier no-axis hypothesis is retained and support conditions are made explicit.
fate: \citet[Theorem 2.5.15]{hormander1971fourier} gives the general inclusion, with the simpler formula after removal of the two axis terms; compare 1973-329.9.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Locally finite configurations and their measurable sets
notes: Configurations are countable subsets \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) without accumulation points; count events \(\mathrm C_{K,j}\) generate the measurable sets. The displayed set mistakenly binds \(K\), not \(X\).
statement: Let \(\Gamma\) be the locally finite simple counting measures on \(\mathbb R^n\), identified with their point sets. Equip \(\Gamma\) with the sigma-algebra generated by \(N_B(X)=|X\cap B|\) for bounded Borel \(B\). For a fixed compact \(K\), \(\mathrm C_{K,j}=\{X\in\Gamma:N_K(X)=j\}\).
fate: The standard measurable configuration formalism appears in \citet[Section 5]{ruelle1970superstable}; the notation in this talk is expository. Simplicity must be changed to integer-valued counting measures when the intensity has atoms.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: The Poisson reference measure
notes: \(\rho(\mathrm C_{K,j})=m(K)^j e^{-m(K)}/j!\), for a locally compact measured space.
statement: For a locally finite diffuse Radon measure \(m\) on a second-countable locally compact space, the Poisson process has independent counts on disjoint bounded Borel sets, and \(N_B\) is Poisson with mean \(m(B)\). On a region \(K\), its symmetric \(j\)-particle measure is \(e^{-m(K)}m^{\otimes j}/j!\), pushed to unordered configurations.
reconstruction: Local finiteness, diffuseness, a standard measurable space, and joint count independence are explicit additions.
fate: This is the usual Poisson reference in \citet[Section 5]{ruelle1970superstable}. Independence of disjoint counts completes the displayed one-set marginal formula; no new probability measure is proposed here.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Finite interaction range gives conditional locality
notes: \ru{Взаимод. конечно}: \ru{независимость}; the sketch separates an inner region from the exterior by a collar of width one.
statement: For a finite-range Gibbs specification, the conditional law inside \(O\), given its entire exterior configuration, depends only on exterior particles within the interaction range of \(O\). Consequently the interior and the farther exterior are conditionally independent given the collar. Unconditional independence does not follow.
fate: The precise conditional-distribution framework was already established by \citet[Section 1]{dobrushin1968conditional}. The next talk supplies the missing conditional-law formula explicitly (1974-355.3--4).
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Finite-range many-particle interaction potentials
notes: \(U(x_1,\ldots,x_j)=0\) if the diameter is at least one. A proposed infinite hard-core value is crossed out.
statement: A symmetric family \(U_j\) is of range one if every \(U_j(x_1,\ldots,x_j)\) vanishes when the set of its arguments has diameter at least one. For a finite configuration, its energy sums \(U_j\) over unordered \(j\)-element subsets. Finite range and finite interaction order are separate conditions.
fate: Finite-range interactions are standard in the conditional specification approach of \citet[Section 1]{dobrushin1968conditional}. The deleted line cannot be used as an assumption; the more explicit pair-potential model appears on P000587.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: The unexplained termination of the potential sequence
notes: \ru{Посл. обрыв., т.к. становится \(\equiv+\infty\)} follows the partially cancelled hard-core clause.
statement: The fragment does not identify which sequence terminates, or whether it means a maximum admissible particle number, a finite list of potentials, or an energy tending to infinity. A hard core bounds the number of particles in a bounded region, but finite interaction range alone does not bound interaction order.
fate: Neither the crossed-out condition nor the following density resolves the intended assertion. Searches in the Dobrushin/Ruelle specification literature did not identify an exact theorem corresponding to this phrase.
present_status: As of November 2026: not identifiable; no open problem is extracted from the cancelled shorthand.

title: Finite-volume Gibbs density and particle-number sectors
notes: The notes write \(d(X)=e^{-\sum U_j}\), call it \(d(\mathrm{Gibbs})/d\mu\), and then use \(m^{\otimes n}\) on \(K^n\).
statement: For a fixed exterior condition \(Y\), define \(dG_K^Y=Z_K(Y)^{-1}e^{-H_K(X\mid Y)}d\Pi_{m,K}(X)\), assuming \(0<Z_K(Y)<\infty\). Conditional on a specified particle number \(n\), one may instead normalize \(e^{-H_K}\) against the symmetric pushforward of \(m^{\otimes n}\). The grand-canonical version includes all \(n\), with \(1/n!\) factors.
reconstruction: The two ensemble interpretations are separated rather than choosing one silently.
fate: \citet[Section 5]{ruelle1970superstable} treats the normalized finite-volume measures and their limits. The notebook omits normalization and passes between labelled coordinates and unordered configurations without specifying the ensemble; P000587 restores the partition function.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Poisson configurations on an infinite measured metric space
notes: The Poisson count formula is repeated on \(\mathbb R^2\), then on \((M,m)\); \(m(M)=\infty\) is the interesting case, with unspecified homogeneity.
statement: Under the standard local-finiteness and diffuseness assumptions of 1974-354.2, infinite total intensity is compatible with a locally finite process. The count in each relatively compact \(O\) has mean \(m(O)\); disjoint counts are independent. Homogeneity is an extra symmetry assumption and is unnecessary for the definition.
fate: This repeats the standard reference process in \citet[Section 5]{ruelle1970superstable}; it does not assert a new existence theorem for arbitrary measurable metric spaces.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Hard-core finite-range pair energy
notes: \(U_1\) is bounded, \(U_2\) symmetric, infinite at distances \(<\varepsilon\) and zero at distances \(\ge r_0\). The intermediate range is unspecified.
statement: For a finite inside configuration \(X\) and exterior \(Y\), use \(H_O(X\mid Y)=\sum_{x\in X}U_1(x)+\sum_{\{x,x'\}\subset X}U_2(x,x')+\sum_{x\in X,y\in Y}U_2(x,y)\). Each inside pair is counted once. A lower bound and appropriate regularity on the annulus \(\varepsilon\le d(x,y)<r_0\) are needed for subsequent existence claims.
fate: \citet[Sections 1 and 5]{ruelle1970superstable} gives stability and regularity conditions for such continuum energies. Hard core and finite range alone are not a complete theorem hypothesis on an arbitrary metric measure space.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: The DLR conditional probability equation
notes: The conditional density in \(O\) is the exponential of the one-body, inside-pair and inside--outside energies, divided by \(\Xi(Y;O)\).
statement: A probability \(\mu\) is Gibbs for a specified energy if, for every bounded region \(O\), its regular conditional law given the outside configuration equals \(\gamma_O(dX\mid Y)=\Xi(Y;O)^{-1}e^{-H_O(X\mid Y)}\Pi_{m,O}(dX)\), for \(\mu\)-almost every \(Y\). Here \(\Xi\) is the integral of the numerator, finite and positive on admissible boundary conditions.
fate: This is the continuum conditional Gibbs formalism already treated in \citet[Section 5]{ruelle1970superstable}; compare the finite-state formulation of \citet[Section 1]{dobrushin1968conditional}. Earlier seminar context: 1970-195.4 and 1970-200.4.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: The boundary collar is sufficient exterior information
notes: Everything depends only on the points of \(Y\) in the \(r_0\)-neighbourhood of \(O\).
statement: For the finite-range pair energy just defined, \(\gamma_O(\,\cdot\mid Y)\) depends only on \(Y\cap\{y\notin O:d(y,O)<r_0\}\). This is the spatial Markov property of the specification, not independence of the unconditioned field.
fate: The assertion follows directly from the displayed energy and is part of the established specification formalism in \citet[Section 1]{dobrushin1968conditional}. It resolves the shorthand in 1974-354.3.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Gelfand interprets conditioning as disintegration
notes: Gelfand invokes a measurable partition and a general Fubini theorem; the measure on exterior configurations is induced by inverse images.
statement: On standard Borel configuration spaces, the restriction map \(r:X\mapsto X\cap O^c\) has a pushforward probability \(r_*\mu\) and a conditional probability kernel \(\mu_Y\), unique \(r_*\mu\)-almost everywhere, satisfying \(\int F\,d\mu=\int(\int F\,d\mu_Y)\,d(r_*\mu)(Y)\). The kernel is supported on the corresponding fibres almost everywhere.
fate: \citet[Section 3.1, pp.~125--129]{rokhlin1949measure}, received 15 July 1947 and published in 1949, proves the canonical conditional-measure construction and essential uniqueness for measurable partitions of Lebesgue spaces. The cited section was read directly. Gelfand's analogy is an expository one; Dobrushin returns to the precise measure-theoretic formulation in record 358.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Consistency for nested regions
notes: A diagram with \(O_2\subset O_1\) accompanies integration over all ways to fill in the smaller missing configuration.
statement: For a Gibbs specification and bounded \(O_2\subset O_1\), \(\gamma_{O_1}\gamma_{O_2}=\gamma_{O_1}\), where kernels act successively on bounded measurable observables. This expresses the tower property and is the compatibility condition required before seeking a global measure.
reconstruction: The kernel identity is a precise reconstruction of the nested-region explanation.
fate: \citet[Section 1]{dobrushin1968conditional} formulates compatible conditional distributions before its existence theorem. The diagram is interpreted using the normalized kernel on the preceding page.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Existence from finite-volume limits
notes: A Gibbs measure exists; exhaust \(M\) by compact \(O_k\), construct measures there and choose a convergent subsequence. The notes call each local configuration space compact.
statement: A verified sufficient continuum theorem is this: for a translation-invariant superstable, lower-regular pair potential with \(\int_{\mathbb R^d}|1-e^{-\beta U(x)}|\,dx<\infty\), the finite-volume free-boundary measures have subsequential local limits giving tempered Gibbs states. In the hard-core model, local particle numbers are bounded on compact closures, but passage through boundaries and discontinuous potentials still needs justification.
reconstruction: Ruelle’s explicit hypotheses replace the unspecified general metric-space claim.
fate: \citet[Theorem 5.5]{ruelle1970superstable} proves the stated version in 1970. The unrestricted configuration space is not compact: arbitrarily many particles or colliding particles obstruct the naive argument. Thus the notebook sketch is not a proof at its stated generality.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under standard stability and regularity assumptions; the notebook’s arbitrary-space compactness argument remains insufficient, not an open existence problem.

title: One-dimensional uniqueness
notes: For \(M=\mathbb R\) with Lebesgue measure, the Gibbs measure is said to be unique.
statement: The intended assertion is uniqueness for the usual one-dimensional finite-range gas at finite positive temperature and activity, with a hard core and bounded finite interaction away from the core. It is not a uniqueness theorem for every measurable pair potential satisfying only the two displayed endpoint values, nor for arbitrary infinite-range interactions.
fate: One-dimensional uniqueness belongs to the earlier Dobrushin--Ruelle theory. \citet[Section 2]{dobrushin1968conditional} contains the finite-state one-dimensional result; the continuum version in precisely the notebook’s scope was not recovered in the checked sources. Compare the older seminar occurrence 1970-195.5.
present_status: As of November 2026: standard one-dimensional finite-range uniqueness is established; the literal missing regularity and interaction assumptions prevent an exact source match here.

title: Uniqueness at sufficiently low activity
notes: For \(U_1=0\) and \(m\le c\) times Lebesgue measure, sufficiently small \(c\) gives uniqueness.
statement: For the translation-invariant superstable, lower-regular continuum pair potentials of 1974-355.7, the tempered Gibbs state is unique at sufficiently small positive activity \(z\). The smallness threshold depends on temperature and the potential. An inhomogeneous intensity dominated by \(c\,dx\) requires a corresponding uniform contraction estimate.
fate: \citet[Theorem 5.7]{ruelle1970superstable} is an exact low-activity theorem for the homogeneous subclass. The notebook’s more general dominated measure is not separately verified here.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Lattice gas with a Bernoulli reference measure
notes: Replace \(\mathbb R^d\) by \(\mathbb Z^d\), \(d\ge2\), and use the symmetric Bernoulli measure on occupation variables.
statement: A simple lattice gas is a spin field \(\eta\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb Z^d}\). On a finite region \(\Lambda\), use the product Bernoulli-\(1/2\) reference and density proportional to \(e^{-\beta H_\Lambda(\eta\mid\xi)}\). A one-site field can absorb a different positive Bernoulli parameter. Finite-range energies define consistent finite-volume kernels.
fate: This is a special case of \citet[Section 1]{dobrushin1968conditional}, published 1968, and the lattice setting of \citet[Section 1]{pirogovsinai1975phase}. The move to \(d\ge2\) prepares phase coexistence.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Weak-interaction or high-temperature uniqueness
notes: For sufficiently small \(U_1,U_2\), the Gibbs measure is unique.
statement: For a finite-alphabet specification on \(\mathbb Z^d\), let \(c_{ij}\) be the supremum total-variation change in the conditional distribution at site \(i\) when only the exterior spin at \(j\) is changed. If \(\sup_i\sum_jc_{ij}<1\), there is at most one Gibbs measure; compactness and quasilocality supply existence. Bounded finite-range interactions satisfy this criterion at sufficiently high temperature.
reconstruction: The dimensionless contraction condition replaces an unspecified norm-smallness assertion.
fate: \citet[Theorem 2]{dobrushin1968conditional} gives the contraction criterion; \citet{dobrushin1968uniqueness} develops uniqueness and phase transitions. Smallness of the one-site field alone is not essential: the dependence on other sites is what is controlled.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Periodic ground configurations and local energy differences
notes: Translation-invariant \(U_1=\alpha\), even \(U_2(x-y)\), periodic configurations, and minimization against finite changes define the ground states.
statement: For a finite-range translation-invariant lattice Hamiltonian, a configuration \(g\) is a ground state if every finite modification \(\eta\) satisfies \(H(\eta)-H(g)\ge0\), where only terms meeting the modified region enter the finite difference. Periodicity is an additional property, not part of the general ground-state definition.
fate: The local-energy definition and periodic reference states are the framework of \citet[Section 1]{pirogovsinai1975phase}. The 1975 talk predates that paper but uses an older standard notion of ground configuration.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: A finite set of periodic reference ground states
notes: \(G(U)\) is taken to be finite, with \(|G(U)|=k\).
statement: The phase-diagram theorem assumes that the model has exactly a specified finite family \(g_1,\ldots,g_k\) of periodic ground configurations, modulo the stated periodicity convention. Finite-range translation invariance does not imply this hypothesis; highly degenerate models can have infinitely many ground configurations.
fate: This is a hypothesis of \citet[Section 1 and Theorem 1]{pirogovsinai1975phase}, not a universal theorem. The exact low-temperature conclusion depends also on Peierls stability and independent perturbations.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Peierls energy cost for defects
notes: A site lies on the boundary if its neighbourhood agrees with no ground state; \(H(X')-H(X)\ge g\,\Gamma(X')\).
statement: Choose a fixed coarse-graining scale large enough to recognize the periodic ground patterns and the interaction range. A bad cube is one not locally matching any reference pattern. The Peierls condition requires the energy excess of a finite perturbation of a ground state to be at least \(\tau>0\) times the number of bad cubes, with \(\tau\) uniform.
reconstruction: The unspecified neighbourhood and boundary cardinality are replaced by the finite-scale definition in the paper.
fate: \citet[Definitions 1.2--1.3]{pirogovsinai1975phase} gives the matching definition. This particular contour stability hypothesis is part of the Pirogov--Sinai theorem announced here and published later in 1975.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Independent parameters unfold the ground-state energies
notes: \(U_\mu=U+\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}\mu_jU^{(j)}\), near \(\mu=0\), and a condition written \(G(U_\mu)\le G(U)\).
statement: Choose \(k-1\) perturbing interactions whose energy-density differences on \(g_1,\ldots,g_k\), relative to one reference state, form a nonsingular \((k-1)\times(k-1)\) matrix. The ensuing theorem is local in this parameter neighbourhood, with the listed periodic ground states as its reference phases. A set of ground states is not numerically ordered.
reconstruction: The nonsingularity condition is recovered from the matched theorem; the ambiguous set inequality is not silently converted into a cardinality bound.
fate: \citet[Definition 1.4 and Theorem 1]{pirogovsinai1975phase} supplies the independence condition. The notebook’s inequality is plausibly shorthand for inclusion/no new reference states, but its intended meaning is not certain.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Low-temperature coexistence and phase-diagram strata
notes: For large \(\beta\), a point \(\mu(\beta)\) has \(k\) Gibbs distributions, \(k\) emanating curves have \(k-1\), and \(\binom{k}{2}\) surfaces have \(k-2\).
statement: Under the finite-state, finite-range, finitely many periodic ground states, Peierls, and independent-perturbation hypotheses, the low-temperature phase diagram near the reference point has a coexistence locus where \(k\) stable periodic pure phases coexist. Its adjacent local strata correspond to subsets of the stable phases, with the expected codimensions. Counts refer to stable pure phases, not all Gibbs probability measures; convex mixtures already give infinitely many measures when two phases coexist.
fate: This is the central match to \citet[Theorem 1]{pirogovsinai1975phase}, with proof continued in \citet{pirogovsinai1976phase}. Both papers were received on 21 April 1975, after this 24 February notebook occurrence, and appeared in 1975 and 1976 respectively. The notebook’s unqualified uniqueness and total-measure count are stronger than the safely matched statement.
present_status: As of November 2026: the Pirogov--Sinai local phase-diagram theory is established. This entry is evidence of an early seminar presentation, not a still-open conjecture; no completeness claim about all nonperiodic or interface Gibbs states is inferred.

title: Gelfand asks for a p-adic Gibbs analogue
notes: \ru{Вопрос Г. Гиббсовские распределения в \(p\)-адическом случае}.
statement: The note asks for a \(p\)-adic analogue but does not say whether the sites, spin space, interaction values, or probability values are \(p\)-adic, or whether existence, uniqueness, phase transitions, or a particular construction is sought. These interpretations lead to different mathematical problems.
fate: No exact specification is recoverable from this question. A concrete later thematic direction is \citet{rozikovkhakimov2013padic}, received 16 October 2012 and published in 2013, whose publisher abstract discusses \(p\)-adic probability-valued Gibbs measures and Markov fields on countable graphs. That is distinct from real-valued Gibbs measures on a \(p\)-adic spatial domain, and the notebook does not choose between such possibilities. No solution of Gelfand's precise intention is asserted.
present_status: As of November 2026: no definite historical problem is recoverable; the broad prompt is not classified as an undeveloped research gap.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Testing wavefront regularity with nonlinear phases
notes: The linear Fourier phase is replaced by \(\Phi\) with \(\Phi'(x_0)=\xi_0\), and the pairing with \(\varphi e^{i\lambda\Phi}\) is rapidly decreasing.
statement: Fix \(\widehat u(\xi)=\langle u,e^{-ix\cdot\xi}\rangle\). Microlocal smoothness at \((x_0,\xi_0)\) is equivalent to rapid decay of \(\langle u,\chi e^{-it\psi}\rangle\) as \(t\to+\infty\), for cutoffs supported sufficiently near \(x_0\) and smooth real phases whose differentials stay in a sufficiently small cone around \(\xi_0\). The estimates are uniform over suitable bounded families of such phases and cutoffs.
reconstruction: A single negative-sign Fourier convention is used here and below; the original convention is not specified.
fate: This is the nonlinear phase form of the Fourier criterion and nonstationary-phase estimates in \citet[Sections 2.3 and 2.5]{hormander1971fourier}. The notebook's plus sign is consistent with the opposite Fourier convention; its missing local and uniform quantifiers require repair.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Defining an oscillatory distribution by cutoff removal
notes: For \(a\in S^m_{1,0}\), \(\langle A,u\rangle=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\int a(x,\theta)e^{i\Phi(x,\theta)}u(x)\chi(\varepsilon\theta)\,dx\,d\theta\).
statement: Let \(\Phi\) be smooth real and positively homogeneous of degree one for \(\theta\ne0\), with \(d_{x,\theta}\Phi\ne0\), and \(a\in S^m_{1,0}\), with harmless smooth extension at bounded \(\theta\). For a smooth compactly supported cutoff \(\chi=1\) near zero, integration by parts defines the indicated distributional limit independently of \(\chi\). Tests are compactly supported in the \(x\)-variables.
reconstruction: The meaning of phase function is supplied explicitly.
fate: \citet[Section 1.2 and Proposition 2.5.7]{hormander1971fourier} contains this construction; compare 1973-329.12--13. Homogeneity and nonvanishing phase differential are part of the phase-function definition, not optional hypotheses.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: The linear-phase delta example
notes: For \(a=1\), \(\Phi=\langle x,\theta\rangle\), the notebook gives \(\langle A,u\rangle=u(0)\).
statement: With ordinary Lebesgue \(d\theta\) and the Fourier convention fixed above, \(\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{ix\cdot\theta}\,d\theta=(2\pi)^n\delta_0\). Thus the stated value \(u(0)\) uses the normalized measure \((2\pi)^{-n}d\theta\). The distribution is concentrated on the critical set \(x=0\).
fate: This is Fourier inversion, the basic example behind \citet[Section 1.2]{hormander1971fourier}. The notebook does not fix its measure normalization, so this is a convention clarification rather than a certain mathematical error.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Removing the nonstationary part of an amplitude
notes: Split \(a=a_1+a_2\) near a point where \(\Phi'_\theta\ne0\); the corresponding \(A_2\) is smooth.
statement: On a closed conic support where \(|\partial_\theta\Phi|\) is bounded away from zero after angular localization, choose a differential operator \(L\) in \(\theta\) with \(Le^{i\Phi}=e^{i\Phi}\). Iterating its transpose improves amplitude integrability and proves that the resulting oscillatory integral is smooth in \(x\).
fate: The nonstationary-phase integration-by-parts method is established in \citet[Section 1.2]{hormander1971fourier}. The conic cutoff in the sketch records localization, not an additional singularity.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: The critical-set bound for the wavefront
notes: \(C_\Phi=\{\Phi'_\theta=0\}\), \(\lambda_\Phi(x,\theta)=(x,\Phi'_x)\), and \(\mathrm{WF}(A)\subset\Lambda_\Phi=\lambda_\Phi(C_\Phi)\).
statement: For a phase and symbol as above, the wavefront of its oscillatory integral is contained in the closed conic set of \((x,\partial_x\Phi(x,\theta))\) with \(\partial_\theta\Phi=0\) and \((x,\theta)\) in the conic support of the amplitude. One takes the relevant closure when supports or charts are not proper.
fate: \citet[Proposition 2.5.7]{hormander1971fourier} is the exact analytic source. The formula is a containment; amplitudes may vanish or cancel, so equality is not automatic.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Nondegenerate phases parametrize Lagrangians
notes: The rank of \((\Phi''_{\theta x},\Phi''_{\theta\theta})\) is \(N\) on \(C_\Phi\); then \(\lambda_\Phi\) is locally a diffeomorphism and \(\Lambda_\Phi\) is conic Lagrangian.
statement: If the \(N\) differentials \(d(\partial_{\theta_j}\Phi)\) are independent on \(C_\Phi\), this critical set is smooth of dimension \(n\). The map \(\lambda_\Phi\) is a conic Lagrangian immersion and locally identifies \(C_\Phi\) with its image. It is not a local diffeomorphism onto the \(2n\)-dimensional cotangent bundle.
fate: This is the standard nondegenerate phase construction in \citet[Section 3.1]{hormander1971fourier}. The notebook's local-diffeomorphism phrase is correct only with the image as target.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Local phase functions for every conic Lagrangian
notes: Conversely every smooth conic Lagrangian can locally be obtained from a nondegenerate phase, and one may take \(N=n\).
statement: Every germ of a smooth conic Lagrangian in \(T^*X\setminus0\), \(\dim X=n\), has a local positively homogeneous nondegenerate phase representation with at most \(n\) phase variables. Additional variables may be introduced by the usual stabilization on a conic chart, with the accompanying amplitude-order shift.
fate: \citet[Section 3.1, especially Theorems 3.1.3 and 3.1.6]{hormander1971fourier} establishes local parametrization and phase equivalence. The statement is local in the Lagrangian, not a claim of one global generating function.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Euler homogeneity proves the Lagrangian condition
notes: On \(C_\Phi\), \(\Phi'_\theta=0\) implies \(\Phi=0\), then \(\Phi'_x\,dx=0\); hence \(\xi\,dx=0\) on the image.
statement: Euler's identity gives \(\Phi=\theta\cdot\partial_\theta\Phi=0\) on \(C_\Phi\). Restricting \(d\Phi\) gives \(\partial_x\Phi\,dx=0\), so the pullback of the Liouville form vanishes. Its exterior derivative therefore vanishes too; together with nondegeneracy and dimension \(n\), the image is Lagrangian.
fate: This is the elementary proof in the phase geometry of \citet[Section 3.1]{hormander1971fourier}. Homogeneity is essential to the stronger vanishing of the Liouville form.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Equivalent phases define the same distribution class
notes: Two phases parametrizing the same \(\Lambda\) produce the same class of \(A\).
statement: The microlocal class \(I^m(X,\Lambda)\) is independent of the chosen nondegenerate parametrization. In Hörmander's normalization a phase with \(N\) variables uses amplitude order \(m+(\dim X-2N)/4\). Changing \(N\) changes that amplitude order; the principal symbol also includes the stationary-phase signature/Maslov and density factors.
reconstruction: The order shift suppressed in the notebook is restored.
fate: \citet[Theorem 3.2.1 and Definition 3.2.2]{hormander1971fourier} supplies the exact phase-invariance theorem. Equal raw amplitude orders for phases with different \(N\) would be incorrect.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Fourier integral kernels and gluing over phase charts
notes: For \(X,Y\), a conic Lagrangian in \(T^*(X\times Y)\setminus0\) gives a kernel by an oscillatory integral; in general use a sum of phase charts.
statement: A Fourier integral kernel is a Lagrangian distribution on \(X\times Y\), locally represented by nondegenerate oscillatory integrals with compatible order. Partitions of unity and locally finite sums produce the global distribution. To extend the resulting operator to compactly supported distribution inputs, exclude the input axis wavefront; proper support controls noncompact inputs.
fate: This is the FIO construction of \citet[Sections 3.2 and 4.1]{hormander1971fourier}. The associated operator relation reverses the sign of the \(Y\)-covector, as already recorded in 1974-353.9.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Kirillov: affine structures on Lagrangian leaves
notes: If a symplectic manifold has a Lagrangian foliation, its leaves carry an invariantly defined affine structure.
statement: For a Lagrangian foliation with tangent bundle \(L\), the symplectic form identifies \(L\) with its annihilator in \(T^*M\). Transporting the Bott partial connection on that annihilator gives a flat torsion-free connection along each leaf. This is an intrinsic affine structure, without a completeness or trivial-holonomy conclusion.
fate: A checked modern formulation and construction are \citet[Proposition 1.9 and Theorem 1.10]{loustausanders2017bilagrangian}, whose introduction attributes the result to Weinstein (1971). The 1971 original was not accessible for direct theorem verification; the modern result was read. The notebook is therefore an expository occurrence, not evidence of priority for Kirillov.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.
speaker: A. A. Kirillov

title: Basic Hamiltonians give parallel commuting fields
notes: For functions constant along the leaves, the covectors \(d\varphi\) correspond to parallel vector fields; these commute.
statement: If \(f\) and \(g\) are locally constant along a Lagrangian foliation, their Hamiltonian fields are tangent to its leaves and \(\{f,g\}=0\); hence they commute. Locally independent basic differentials give a parallel frame for the leafwise affine connection. Such a frame need not be globally single-valued or complete.
fate: This is the Hamiltonian description accompanying \citet[Theorem 1.10]{loustausanders2017bilagrangian}. The notebook calls the vectors gradients, but the construction uses the symplectic isomorphism, not a Riemannian metric.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.
speaker: A. A. Kirillov

title: The asserted Euclidean-or-torus leaf dichotomy
notes: \ru{Следствие: слои --- \(\mathbb R^n\) или торы}. An uncertain abbreviation follows as an example of a Lagrangian foliation.
statement: The dichotomy is false. For \(T^*(S^1\times\mathbb R)\) with the standard form, the leaves with both momenta constant are Lagrangian cylinders \(S^1\times\mathbb R\). An affine structure alone gives no such topological classification. A connected leaf with \(n\) globally independent complete commuting fields is instead \(\mathbb R^n/\Gamma\), with discrete \(\Gamma\), hence may have any cylinder rank.
fate: The leafwise result verified in \citet[Theorem 1.10]{loustausanders2017bilagrangian} does not assert the notebook corollary. The editorial counterexample is checked in the mathematical audit. The following abbreviation likely denotes a cotangent bundle (\ru{кокасательное расслоение}); it should not be turned into a person named Kokas.
present_status: As of November 2026: the literal corollary is false; the affine-connection theorem is established, and no open classification problem is inferred.
speaker: A. A. Kirillov

title: Recognizing FIOs by rapidly oscillating tests
notes: A kernel whose wavefront lies in \(\Lambda\) and which acts well on transverse oscillating exponentials is an FIO; an asymptotic series is sketched.
statement: For a classical Lagrangian distribution of order \(m\) on a \(d\)-manifold, pairings with \(\chi e^{-it\psi}\), where \(\operatorname{graph}(d\psi)\) meets \(\Lambda\) transversely, have stationary-phase expansions with leading scale \(t^{m-d/4}\) and phase values at the intersections. A converse requires uniform symbol estimates in test-phase parameters, not merely a separate pointwise asymptotic for each \(\psi\).
fate: \citet[Theorems 3.2.4--3.2.5 and the following characterization paragraph]{hormander1971fourier} establishes the forward statement and describes the converse. Record 357 repeats the question explicitly. The notebook suppresses the symbol order and essential uniformity.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: FIO operator action on compactly supported distributions
notes: The oscillatory kernel formula is repeated, with \(A:\mathcal E'(Y)\to\mathcal D'(X)\).
statement: A distribution kernel represented by nondegenerate phase charts defines this extension when its wavefront avoids covectors \((x,0;y,\eta)\), \(\eta\ne0\). The other axis condition gives smooth output on smooth test inputs. Merely being a Lagrangian distribution on \(X\times Y\) does not ensure both operator properties.
fate: This is the combination of \citet[Theorems 2.5.12--2.5.14 and Section 4.1]{hormander1971fourier}, already discussed in 1974-353.8 and 1974-356.10.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Pseudodifferential operators as diagonal FIOs
notes: In the PDO case \(\Lambda=\{(x,\xi;x,-\xi)\}\).
statement: The unprimed kernel relation of a pseudodifferential operator is contained in the nonzero conormal bundle of the diagonal. After reversing the input covector, it becomes the identity relation on \(T^*X\setminus0\). Classical symbols produce the familiar oscillatory kernel with phase \((x-y)\cdot\xi\).
fate: \citet[Section 4.1]{hormander1971fourier} places pseudodifferential operators in the FIO class. Earlier occurrences include 1971-234.3 and 1973-329.5--7.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Gelfand asks for a p-adic FIO construction
notes: \ru{Вопрос Г.: хорошо бы в \(p\)-адическом случае построить}. The intended object is the just-discussed calculus.
statement: The notes request a non-Archimedean analogue without specifying a field, character, symbol class, canonical relations, or closure operations. There is no unique exact theorem to match. A later concrete analogue uses distributional wavefront sets over a \(p\)-adic field and oscillatory integrals with a fixed additive character.
fate: \citet[Sections 1--2]{heifetz1985padic}, published in 1985, constructs a \(p\)-adic wavefront theory and stationary-phase methods, including pullbacks, products and kernel operations. This is a substantial thematic continuation, but it does not establish that a particular full FIO calculus requested here was completed. No exact solution date is assigned.
present_status: As of November 2026: relevant non-Archimedean microlocal theories exist, but the notebook prompt is too underspecified to classify as a solved or unsolved definite problem.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: When is a distribution kernel a Fourier integral kernel?
notes: Tulovskii answers: wavefront inside a Lagrangian, and transverse exponential tests have an asymptotic expansion determined by that Lagrangian.
statement: A precise recognition problem is to characterize classical Lagrangian distributions \(I^m_{\mathrm{cl}}(X\times Y,\Lambda)\) by their pairings with localized transverse oscillatory tests, uniformly in smooth phase families and with the order \(m-(\dim X+\dim Y)/4\) prescribed. Wavefront containment alone does not characterize this class; singular amplitudes of arbitrary order can have the same wavefront set.
fate: \citet[Theorems 3.2.4--3.2.5 and the following paragraph]{hormander1971fourier} already gives the asymptotic test framework and explicitly indicates its converse characterization. The question repeats 1974-356.14 and is expository, with missing uniform symbol bounds rather than an identified research gap.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Microlocal straightening of a real principal symbol
notes: For an order-one PDO with real \(p\), \(p(x_0,\xi_0)=0\), and \(dp(x_0,\xi_0)\ne0\), there are FIOs \(A,B\) with \(P\equiv B\partial_{X_n}A\) and \(BA\equiv I\) microlocally.
statement: The standard homogeneous FIO normal form additionally requires that \(H_p\) not be tangent to the radial cone direction at the point. For a classical order-one operator of real principal type under that nonradial condition, elliptic local FIOs quantizing inverse homogeneous canonical transformations conjugate \(P\), modulo smoothing terms, to \(D_{X_n}=-i\partial_{X_n}\), with harmless elliptic factors according to normalization.
fate: \citet[Proposition 6.1.4 and its application]{duistermaathormander1972fourierii} explicitly includes the nonradial hypothesis. The notebook omits it. The symbol \(p=x\xi\) at \((0,1)\) has \(dp\ne0\) but radial Hamiltonian field, and cannot be straightened to a nonradial coordinate symbol by a homogeneous canonical transformation; see the audit.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified normal-form theorem is established; the dp-only homogeneous formulation is false.

title: Propagation of singularities for real principal type
notes: For \(Pu=f\), \(\mathrm{WF}(u)\setminus\mathrm{WF}(f)\subset\{p=0\}\) and it is invariant under \(H_p=\sum(p_{x_j}\partial_{\xi_j}-p_{\xi_j}\partial_{x_j})\).
statement: For a scalar classical PDO with real homogeneous principal symbol of principal type, elliptic regularity gives \(\mathrm{WF}(u)\setminus\mathrm{WF}(Pu)\subset\operatorname{Char}(P)\). In the open complement of \(\mathrm{WF}(Pu)\), this set is a union of bicharacteristic segments of the principal Hamilton field. Invariance is understood only while the segment stays in that open region; it does not continue through singular forcing without qualification.
reconstruction: The principal-type scope and restriction to nonsingular forcing are made explicit.
fate: \citet[Theorem 6.1.1]{duistermaathormander1972fourierii} is the published 1972 result. The notebook's Hamilton field is the negative of the common convention, which reverses orientation but not the unparameterized bicharacteristics.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Bernstein: characteristic variety of an operator ideal
notes: The \(\mathrm{WF}\) of a left ideal of polynomial-coefficient differential operators is the common zero set of its principal symbols.
statement: Over a characteristic-zero field, let \(D\) be the Weyl algebra and \(I\subsetneq D\) a left ideal. With the order filtration and its induced good quotient filtration, \(\operatorname{Char}(D/I)\subset T^*\mathbb A^n\) is the zero set of \(\operatorname{gr}I\). Symbols of all elements of \(I\), not merely an arbitrary generating list, must be used. The zero section is retained.
fate: \citet[Section 1, Definition 1.6]{bernstein1971modules} develops characteristic carriers for differential-operator modules. The word \(\mathrm{WF}\) here is an algebraic analogy, not the smooth wavefront of one distribution.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.
speaker: I. N. Bernstein

title: Bernstein’s lower bound on characteristic dimension
notes: \(\dim\mathrm{WF}\ge\dim X\).
statement: For a nonzero finitely generated Weyl-algebra module over a characteristic-zero field, its dimension is at least \(n\). For the order characteristic variety of \(D/I\), this gives \(\dim\operatorname{Char}(D/I)\ge n\). The hypothesis \(I\ne D\) is essential; no corresponding assertion holds for the empty characteristic variety of the zero module.
fate: \citet[Theorem 1.3, proved in Section 5]{bernstein1972continuation} proves the dimension inequality; the paper was submitted on 21 June 1972 and published in 1972. The 1971 paper supplies the filtered-module framework, not the exact inequality locator. A modern full order-characteristic statement is \citet[Theorem 3.38]{mustata2023dmodules}. Thus the 1975 intervention is expository.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.
speaker: I. N. Bernstein

title: Finite-spin random fields
notes: \(X\) is finite, \(T\) countable, and a random field is a probability measure on \(X^T\); the physical interpretation is a spin system.
statement: Equip the finite alphabet \(X\) with its discrete sigma-algebra and \(X^T\) with the product sigma-algebra. A probability law there defines the coordinate random variables \(\eta_t\); conversely their consistent finite-dimensional laws determine that probability uniquely. No Gibbs property is part of this definition.
fate: This is the starting framework of \citet[Section 1]{dobrushin1968conditional}; its use in the notebook is exposition of established probability theory.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Point random fields
notes: Realizations are subsets of \(\mathbb R^\nu\) meeting every bounded region in finitely many points; a measure on realizations is a point random field.
statement: A simple locally finite point field is a probability measure on the configuration space with the count-generated sigma-algebra from 1974-354.1. Local finiteness applies to relatively compact Borel regions; integer-valued counting measures allow multiplicity when desired.
fate: The continuum configuration framework is explicitly used in \citet[Section 5]{ruelle1970superstable}. This repeats Sinai's model while distinguishing it from a field with a fixed site set.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Generalized random fields valued in distributions
notes: The third object is a probability measure on \(\mathcal S^*(\mathbb R^\nu)\), linked to quantum field theory.
statement: A tempered generalized random field may be represented by a probability measure on \(\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^\nu)\), with evaluation maps \(u\mapsto\langle u,\varphi\rangle\) measurable for every Schwartz test function. Such a field need not admit pointwise values. The mere definition does not construct a measure for an interacting quantum field model.
fate: \citet[Section 1]{minlos1959generalized} develops generalized random processes and their extension to measures. Its main results were reported on 11 April 1958 and published in 1959, well before this session. The notes offer only the object definition and motivation.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: The Markov-chain comparison
notes: The notes write \(\Pr(x_n\mid x_k,\ k\le n)=\Pr(x_n\mid x_{n-1})\).
statement: The Markov property is \(\Pr(X_n\in A\mid\sigma(X_k:k<n))=\Pr(X_n\in A\mid X_{n-1})\) almost surely. The conditioning must exclude \(X_n\) itself; conditioning on \(\sigma(X_k:k\le n)\) gives the indicator of \(X_n\in A\), and does not express the usual Markov property.
fate: The chain analogy in \citet[Section 1]{dobrushin1968conditional} motivates finite-range spatial conditional distributions. The scan clearly has \(k\le n\), so the inequality is a faithful notebook error, not an uncertain transcription.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Construct all fields with prescribed exterior conditional laws
notes: The problem is to prescribe, for each finite \(V\subset T\), the conditional distribution in \(V\) given the configuration in \(T\setminus V\), then construct the corresponding field measures.
statement: Given a proper consistent family of probability kernels \((\gamma_V)_{V\Subset T}\) on \(X^T\), determine the set \(\mathcal G(\gamma)=\{\mu:\mu\gamma_V=\mu\text{ for every finite }V\}\), including whether it is nonempty and when it has one element. For finite \(X\) and countable \(T\), quasilocality of a specification suffices for nonemptiness. A contraction condition such as 1974-355.11 gives uniqueness; coexistence shows it is not automatic.
fate: \citet[Section 1 and Theorems 1--2]{dobrushin1968conditional}, received 20 April 1967 and published in 1968, formulates this exact inverse problem and proves these sufficient existence/uniqueness results. The 1975 statement is an expository programme; it is not a claim that every compatible measurable specification has a universal simple classification.
present_status: As of November 2026: the finite-alphabet quasilocal existence and weak-dependence uniqueness statements are established. The general classification remains a model-dependent programme, not a single unresolved conjecture extracted from this entry.

title: Regular conditional probability as a measurable kernel
notes: For a sub-sigma-algebra, conditional probabilities are probability measures depending measurably on the conditioning data and satisfying an integral identity.
statement: A regular conditional probability of \(\mu\) given \(\mathcal B\subset\mathcal A\) is a probability kernel \(K(\omega,A)\) such that \(K(\cdot,A)\) is \(\mathcal B\)-measurable and \(\int_BK(\omega,A)\,\mu(d\omega)=\mu(A\cap B)\) for every \(A\in\mathcal A,B\in\mathcal B\). For each fixed \(A\), it is a version of \(\mathbb E_\mu[1_A\mid\mathcal B]\).
fate: This is the kernel form of the canonical systems in \citet[Section 3.1, pp.~125--129]{rokhlin1949measure}. The defining identities are meaningful independently of whether such a probability-valued version exists on an arbitrary space.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Existence and almost-everywhere uniqueness of conditional kernels
notes: In a broad class of cases, regular conditional probabilities exist and are unique.
statement: For a probability on a standard Borel space and conditioning by a measurable map to another standard Borel space, a disintegration exists and is unique outside a set of conditioning values of pushforward measure zero. In equivalent countably generated conditioning formulations the same almost-everywhere qualification applies. Pointwise uniqueness on null fibres is false.
fate: \citet[Section 3.1, pp.~125--129]{rokhlin1949measure} proves existence for measurable partitions of Lebesgue spaces and essential uniqueness. Received 15 July 1947, it appeared in Russian in 1949. The notebook's broad-class phrase is correct but supplies neither the space hypotheses nor the null-set qualification.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Fubini’s theorem as conditional measure on a rectangle
notes: For the square with planar Lebesgue measure, conditioning on a vertical coordinate gives Lebesgue measure along the corresponding segment.
statement: On \([0,1]^2\) with product Lebesgue probability and projection \((x,y)\mapsto x\), a disintegration is \(K_x=\delta_x\otimes dy\). Hence \(\int F(x,y)\,dx\,dy=\int(\int F(x,y)\,dy)\,dx\) for integrable \(F\). The explicit kernel can be chosen for every \(x\), although uniqueness is only almost everywhere.
fate: This is the elementary product example of \citet[Section 3.1]{rokhlin1949measure}; it explains the general-Fubini remark already made by Gelfand in 1974-355.5.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Conditioning on a map or a countable family of observables
notes: A measurable \(\xi:X\to F\) defines the conditioning partition; a countable collection of real functions can be treated similarly.
statement:
For standard Borel \(X,F\) and measurable \(\xi\), define \(
u=\xi_*\mu\). Conditional kernels \(K_y\) satisfy \(\mu(A)=\int_FK_y(A)\,
u(dy)\) and are concentrated on \(\xi^{-1}(y)\) for \(
u\)-almost every \(y\). A countable sequence \((\xi_j)\) is a single map into the standard Borel product \(\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}\).
fate: The measurable partitions generated by one or countably many real functions are explicit examples in \citet[Section 3.1, p.~126]{rokhlin1949measure}. This closes the foundational loop needed for Gibbs exterior conditioning.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Particle-like structures in theories with broken symmetry
notes: Polyakov discusses spontaneously broken symmetry and describes particles as bubbles in the ether of quantum field theory, followed by a list of researchers.
statement: The recoverable mathematical theme is that nonlinear field configurations may carry particle-like localized energy and nontrivial topology. The note gives no field space, gauge group, energy functional, boundary conditions, stability criterion, or topological charge, and therefore specifies no particular existence or classification result.
fate: Polyakov's \citet{polyakov1974particle} is an obvious contemporary primary lead: its 1974 publication predates this talk. Nielsen--Olesen vortices are another distinct lead. The names and metaphor do not license importing either complete model into the notebook. The institutional publication record verifies Polyakov's title and date, but an exact notebook-to-theorem match cannot be established.

title: Two programmes for holomorphic mapping theory
notes: The opening lists hyperbolic analysis, in which negative curvature restricts holomorphic maps, and counting volumes of divisors by residue calculus.
statement: These are two announced methods, not two quantified conjectures: differential inequalities for maps into targets with suitably negative curvature, and current identities that compare divisor counting with growth. The first is made precise in record 361; the second is developed in the present talk.
fate: \citet[Sections 1, 5, and Appendix]{griffithsking1973nevanlinna} contains both parts of this programme. The note does not assert that every notion of negative curvature yields the same mapping restriction.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Logarithmic residue as integration around a normal circle
notes: The notes write \(\eta=(dg/2\pi ig)\wedge\zeta+\xi\), then \(\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\int_{C(\varepsilon)}\eta=\zeta|_D\), calling \(\eta\) an arbitrary form off \(D=\{g=0\}\).
statement: If \(D\) is a smooth reduced hypersurface, \(dg\ne0\) along \(D\), and \(\zeta,\xi\) are smooth forms of degrees \(r-1,r\), the displayed logarithmic form has residue \(\zeta|_D\). The limit is integration along the positively oriented normal circle fibres of a shrinking tube. Over an \((r-1)\)-cycle \(c\subset D\), it reads \(\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\int_{\operatorname{tube}_\varepsilon(c)}\eta=\int_c\zeta\). An arbitrary form on the complement need not admit this logarithmic decomposition.
reconstruction: Fibre integration distinguishes the form-valued residue from a scalar integral over a whole cycle.
fate: The local residue/current method is the one used in \citet[Section 1(a), especially Proposition 1.1]{griffithsking1973nevanlinna}. The tube description is a standard local interpretation of the logarithmic model; the notebook suppresses the smooth-divisor and simple-pole assumptions.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Currents and their distributional exterior derivative
notes: A current is a functional on compactly supported forms; an \(L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}\) form \(\lambda\) gives \([\lambda](\varphi)=\int\lambda\wedge\varphi\), and \(dT(\varphi)=\pm T(d\varphi)\).
statement: On an oriented real \(2n\)-manifold, a degree-\(r\) current is a continuous linear functional on compactly supported smooth \((2n-r)\)-forms. For a locally integrable \(r\)-form, \([\lambda]\) is defined by integration and \(dT(\varphi)=(-1)^{r+1}T(d\varphi)\). A smooth oriented submanifold defines an integration current of degree its real codimension.
fate: These conventions are introduced in \citet[Section 1(a)]{griffithsking1973nevanlinna}. The missing continuity and degree convention are supplied; the notebook explicitly leaves the sign open rather than giving a wrong fixed sign.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: The residue current measures the singular part of differentiation
notes: For a locally integrable form smooth off the exceptional set, \(\operatorname{Res}\eta=d[\eta]-[d\eta]=[\zeta|_D]\).
statement: Suppose \(\eta\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}\) is smooth off \(D\), and its ordinary derivative there also has a locally integrable extension \(d_{\mathrm{reg}}\eta\). Then \(d[\eta]-[d_{\mathrm{reg}}\eta]\) is supported on \(D\). For the logarithmic model of 1974-360.2 it equals the pushforward \(i_*[\zeta|_D]\), where \(i:D\hookrightarrow V\). The second integrability requirement is necessary to make the difference meaningful in this form.
reconstruction: The notation distinguishes the current derivative from the ordinary derivative on the complement.
fate: The Poincaré--Lelong current calculation of \citet[Proposition 1.1 and its proof]{griffithsking1973nevanlinna} gives the model. No assertion that every locally integrable form has a locally integrable ordinary derivative is valid.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: The one-variable residue normalization
notes: For \(\eta=dz/z\), the notes give \(d[\eta](\varphi)-[\eta](d\varphi)=\lim\int\varphi\,dz=\varphi(0)\).
statement: With the current convention in 1974-360.3 and counterclockwise circles, \(d[dz/z]=2\pi i\,\delta_0\), while the ordinary derivative of \(dz/z\) is zero off the origin. Equivalently \(d[dz/(2\pi iz)]=\delta_0\). The contour integrand is \(\varphi\,dz/z\). For a degree-one current, \(d[\eta](\varphi)=[\eta](d\varphi)\), so the notebook's written left-hand difference is identically zero.
fate: This is the elementary one-variable calculation underlying \citet[Proposition 1.1]{griffithsking1973nevanlinna}. The scan confirms the missing denominator/normalization and the wrong second term; these are faithful notebook errors.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: The divisor residue includes vanishing multiplicities
notes: For holomorphic \(g\), \(\operatorname{Res}[dg/(2\pi ig)]=[Z]\), with \(Z=\sum m_iZ_i\) and \(m_i=\operatorname{ord}_{Z_i}g\).
statement: If \(g\) is a nonzero holomorphic function on a complex manifold, its divisor is \(\operatorname{div}(g)=\sum_i m_iZ_i\). As currents, \(dd^c\log|g|^2=\sum_i m_i[Z_i]\), with \(d^c=(i/4\pi)(\bar\partial-\partial)\). Equivalently the logarithmic differential has this residue current. The weights are part of the divisor; the reduced zero set alone loses them.
fate: \citet[Proposition 1.1, equation (1.2)]{griffithsking1973nevanlinna} is an exact Poincaré--Lelong match. The statement includes singular zero sets, via their integration currents.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: A divisor determines a line bundle and canonical section
notes: Local equations \(g_i\) for a codimension-one \(X\subset V\) give ratios \(f_{ij}=g_i/g_j\), a bundle \(L_X\), and a section \(\sigma=\{g_i\}\) vanishing on \(X\).
statement: For an effective Cartier divisor \(D\) on a complex manifold, local equations with invertible holomorphic ratios define \(\mathcal O(D)\) and its canonical holomorphic section \(\sigma\), whose divisor is \(D\). A bare subset of codimension one is insufficient: it must be an analytic divisor with its multiplicities. Frame-transition conventions determine whether one writes the ratio or its reciprocal.
fate: The divisor and metric setup used by \citet[Sections 0(a) and 1(c)]{griffithsking1973nevanlinna} is exactly this construction. The notebook suppresses the analytic/Cartier and transition-convention qualifications.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: The Hermitian Poincaré--Lelong identity and its sign
notes: For \(\|\sigma\|^2=h_i|g_i|^2\), the notes put \(\eta=(2\pi i)^{-1}\partial\log\|\sigma\|^2\), identify \([d\eta]\) with \(c(L_D)\), and later write \([D]=d[\eta]+[c(L_D)]\).
statement: Fix \(d^c=(i/4\pi)(\bar\partial-\partial)\), so \(dd^c=(i/2\pi)\partial\bar\partial\). If \(h=\|e\|^2\) in a holomorphic frame, \(c_1(L,h)=-dd^c\log h\). For a nonzero holomorphic section, \(dd^c\log\|\sigma\|^2=[D]-c_1(L,h)\). Thus the ordinary \(d\eta\) off \(D\), for the notebook's \(\eta\), is \(-c_1(L,h)\), whereas the current derivative has the additional \([D]\) term.
fate: \citet[Proposition 1.14]{griffithsking1973nevanlinna} gives the global current identity. The notebook's two sign assignments are inconsistent under a fixed Chern-form convention; the later \([D]=d[\eta]+c_1\) has the standard sign.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: The divisor class is Poincaré dual to the first Chern class
notes: The current de Rham theorem identifies the zero-set current with the Chern class; for closed \(\psi\), \(\int_D\psi=\int_Vc(L_D)\wedge\psi\).
statement: For a divisor \(D\) on a compact complex \(n\)-manifold, its current cohomology class equals \(c_1(\mathcal O(D))\). Consequently, for a closed smooth \((2n-2)\)-form \(\psi\), \(\int_D\psi=\int_Vc_1(\mathcal O(D),h)\wedge\psi\), counting divisor multiplicities. On a noncompact manifold, take compactly supported test forms or otherwise justify all integrals and boundary terms.
fate: This is the cohomological interpretation immediately after \citet[Proposition 1.14, pp.~162--163]{griffithsking1973nevanlinna}. It is already established before the talk.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Bézout by products of divisor classes
notes: For two curves in \(\mathbb P^2\), the notes identify the number of intersection points with the product of Chern classes and obtain \(d_Xd_Y\).
statement: For plane projective curves \(X,Y\) over \(\mathbb C\) with no common irreducible component, the sum of local intersection multiplicities is \(\deg X\,\deg Y\). With a hyperplane form \(\omega\) normalized by \(\int_{\mathbb P^2}\omega^2=1\), the cohomological product is \((\deg X)(\deg Y)\int\omega^2\). It counts distinct points only when every intersection is transverse. The product of arbitrary singular currents is not automatically defined; here one uses proper algebraic intersection or an appropriate regularization.
fate: The divisor-current and proper-intersection formalism of \citet[Section 1(c), Propositions 1.14--1.15]{griffithsking1973nevanlinna} supplies the argument. The notebook omits properness and multiplicities in the phrase 'number of points'. This is classical exposition, not a new proof claiming priority.

title: Integration currents on singular analytic sets
notes: The notes say the theorem remains valid for \(X\) with singularities, followed by 'Lelong, 1953'.
statement: For a pure-dimensional analytic set \(X\), integration over its regular locus has locally finite mass and extends to a closed positive current \([X]\) on the ambient manifold. Analytic cycles are handled by summing these currents with their multiplicities. This justifies the divisor-current formulas even when the divisor is singular; it does not define arbitrary products of such currents.
fate: \citet[Theorems 7--8, pp.~257--258]{lelong1957integration} proves the integration-current extension and additivity; the paper is from 1957. Its bibliography includes a 1953 Lelong contribution, but the notebook's precise 1953 attribution was not verified. The checked 1957 publication is sufficient to establish that the result predates the seminar.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Pullback volume counts the multiplicity of a holomorphic map
notes: For \(f:\mathbb C^n\to V\) with compact Kähler target, \(\operatorname{vol}(f(B(r)))=\int_{B(r)}f^*(\omega^n)\).
statement: The integral \(n!^{-1}\int_{B(r)}f^*\omega^n\) is the parametrized \(2n\)-dimensional volume of \(f\), counting local covering multiplicity. It equals the ordinary image volume only under suitable almost-everywhere injectivity; it vanishes where the complex rank is below \(n\). The factor \(n!\) is omitted if volume is defined using \(\omega^n\) itself.
fate: \citet[Section 5(a)--(b)]{griffithsking1973nevanlinna} uses these pullback growth integrals. The notebook's equality needs the multiplicity interpretation; it is not an identity for unweighted images of arbitrary maps.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is an expository occurrence, not a new open problem.

title: Graph volume and the mixed raw growth integrals
notes: For the graph above \(B(r)\), the notes expand \(\int_{\Gamma(r)}(\varphi+\omega)^n\) and define \(T_k(f,r)=\int_{B(r)}\varphi^{n-k}\wedge f^*(\omega^k)\).
statement: Let \(\omega_0\) be the Euclidean Kähler form and put \(t_k(f,r)=\int_{B(r)}\omega_0^{n-k}\wedge f^*\omega^k\), \(0\le k\le n\). Then \(n!\operatorname{Vol}(\Gamma_f|_{B(r)})=\sum_{k=0}^n\binom nk t_k(f,r)\) for the product metric. These are raw ball integrals; a Nevanlinna characteristic is obtained by an additional radial integration and normalization.
reconstruction: The lower-case notation is editorial, explicitly separating two quantities denoted T in the notebook.
fate: The graph-growth method and higher characteristic forms are discussed in \citet[Section 5, pp.~180--183]{griffithsking1973nevanlinna}. Changing the notebook's raw \(T_k\) to \(t_k\) here prevents confusion with the integrated characteristic on the next page.

title: The unspecified comparison of higher growth with first growth
notes: The notes say 'in many cases' \(T_k=O(T_1)\), adding 'of one order'.
statement: No family of maps, target hypothesis, range of \(k\), or choice between raw and integrated characteristics is specified. Therefore the phrase gives no definite universal estimate. The graph-volume identity by itself does not imply domination of every higher mixed integral by the first.
fate: \citet[Section 5(b), pp.~182--183]{griffithsking1973nevanlinna} discusses the different higher growth quantities and the difficulty of reducing their information to first growth. This is thematic support for the surrounding subject, not verification of an unqualified \(O\)-estimate. No exact source or modern open question is assigned to 'many cases'.
